issues.title: slug() should drop accents
issues.body: `slug('Crème Brûlée')` returns `cr-me-br-l-e`. It should return `creme-brulee`.

issues.title: Add a strip_html() helper
issues.body:
Add `strip_html(text)` that removes HTML tags and decodes entities: `strip_html('

Fish & chips

')` should return `Fish & chips`.

issues.title: wrap() should not split URLs
issues.body: `wrap()` breaks long URLs across lines, which makes them unclickable. A URL should stay on one line even when it is longer than the width.

issues.title: Add a wrap command to the CLI
issues.body: `python -m textkit wrap --width 40 "some text"` should print the wrapped text.

issues.title: count_words() should count CJK characters as words
issues.body: `count_words('我喜欢猫')` returns 1. Each CJK character should count as one word, so it should return 4.

issues.title: Retry when the server answers 503
issues.body: `fetch_json` should retry up to 3 times when the server answers 503, waiting a little between tries.

issues.title: Cache responses on disk
issues.body: Add an optional on-disk cache: `fetch_json(url, cache_dir=path)` returns the cached body for 60 seconds instead of fetching again.

issues.title: Colour the JSON output
issues.body: The CLI should print the JSON with syntax colours when standard output is a terminal.

issues.title: Read the config from a TOML file
issues.body: `config.load` should also accept a `fetchit.toml` file with a `[fetchit]` table.

issues.title: Validate the response against a JSON Schema
issues.body: Add `fetch_json(url, schema=...)`: it raises `FetchError` when the JSON does not match the given JSON Schema.

issues.title: slug() should transliterate German letters
issues.body: `slug('Größe Über')` should return `grosse-uber` (ß becomes ss, umlauts lose their dots).
issues.check:
from textkit import slug
assert slug('Größe Über') == 'grosse-uber', slug('Größe Über')

issues.title: Add a sanitize_html() helper
issues.body: Add `sanitize_html(text)` that keeps only `` and `` tags and removes every other tag, keeping the text: `sanitize_html('x')` should return `xy`.
issues.check: import textkit f = getattr(textkit, 'sanitize_html', None) or __import__('textkit.core', fromlist=['x']).sanitize_html out = f('x') assert 'x' in out and '

issues.title: truncate() should not cut inside a word
issues.body: `truncate('hello wonderful world', 12)` returns `hello wonde…`. It should cut at the last whole word: `hello…`.
issues.check:
from textkit import truncate
out = truncate('hello wonderful world', 12)
assert out.endswith('\u2026') and 'wonde' not in out and out.startswith('hello'), out

issues.title: Add a title command to the CLI
issues.body: `python -m textkit title "hello world"` should print `Hello World`.
issues.check:
import subprocess, sys
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'textkit', 'title', 'hello world'], capture_output=True, text=True)
assert r.stdout.strip() == 'Hello World', (r.stdout, r.stderr)

issues.title: count_words() should skip punctuation-only tokens
issues.body: `count_words('hello , world !')` returns 4. Tokens made only of punctuation are not words: it should return 2.
issues.check:
from textkit import count_words
assert count_words('hello , world !') == 2

issues.title: wrap() should measure wide characters
issues.body: CJK characters take two columns in a terminal, but `wrap()` counts them as one, so lines come out twice as wide as asked. `wrap()` should count a wide character as two columns.
issues.check:
from textkit import wrap
lines = wrap('猫' * 10, 10).split('\n')
assert all(len(l) <= 5 for l in lines) and ''.join(lines) == '猫' * 10, lines

issues.title: Add a detect_encoding() helper
issues.body: Add `detect_encoding(data: bytes) -> str` that returns the text encoding of `data`: `utf-8` for UTF-8 text, `utf-16` for UTF-16 with a byte order mark.
issues.check:
import textkit
f = getattr(textkit, 'detect_encoding', None) or __import__('textkit.core', fromlist=['x']).detect_encoding
assert f('héllo'.encode('utf-8')).lower().replace('_', '-') in ('utf-8', 'utf8'), f('héllo'.encode('utf-8'))
assert f(b'\xff\xfeh\x00i\x00').lower().replace('_', '-').startswith('utf-16')

issues.title: slug() should accept a separator
issues.body: `slug('Hello World', sep='_')` should return `hello_world`. The default stays `-`.
issues.check:
from textkit import slug
assert slug('Hello World', sep='_') == 'hello_world' and slug('Hello World') == 'hello-world'

issues.title: Add a strip_markdown() helper
issues.body: Add `strip_markdown(text)` that removes emphasis and inline code marks: `strip_markdown('**bold** and _it_ and `code`')` should return `bold and it and code`.
issues.check:
import textkit
f = getattr(textkit, 'strip_markdown', None) or __import__('textkit.core', fromlist=['x']).strip_markdown
assert f('**bold** and _it_ and `code`') == 'bold and it and code', f('**bold** and _it_ and `code`')

issues.title: title_case() should keep small words lowercase
issues.body: `title_case('the lord of the rings')` returns `The Lord Of The Rings`. Small words (of, the, a, an, and, in, on) after the first word should stay lowercase: `The Lord of the Rings`.
issues.check:
from textkit import title_case
assert title_case('the lord of the rings') == 'The Lord of the Rings'

issues.title: Retry with backoff on connection errors
issues.body: When the connection fails (`URLError`), `fetch_json` should try again, up to 3 tries in all, waiting longer after each failure.

issues.title: Support HTTP basic auth
issues.body: `fetch_json(url, auth=('user', 'secret'))` should send an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header.

issues.title: Send extra headers
issues.body: `fetch_json(url, headers={'X-Team': 'a'})` should send the given headers, and the CLI should take `--header 'Name: value'` (repeatable).

issues.title: Show a list as a table
issues.body: `fetchit URL --table` should print a JSON list of objects as an aligned text table, one row per object and one column per key.
issues.check:
import io, contextlib
import fetchit.cli as C
C.fetch_json = lambda url, **kw: [{'a': 1, 'b': 2}, {'a': 3, 'b': 4}]
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    rc = C.main(['http://x.invalid/', '--table'])
out = buf.getvalue()
assert rc == 0 and 'a' in out and '3' in out and '{' not in out, out

issues.title: Colour error messages red
issues.body: When standard error is a terminal, the CLI should print its error message in red. The exit code stays 1.
issues.check:
import io, sys
import fetchit.cli as C
class TTY(io.StringIO):
    def isatty(self): return True
def boom(url, **kw): raise C.FetchError('nope')
C.fetch_json = boom
err = TTY()
real, sys.stderr = sys.stderr, err
try:
    rc = C.main(['http://x.invalid/'])
finally:
    sys.stderr = real
out = err.getvalue()
assert rc == 1 and 'nope' in out and '\x1b[' in out, repr(out)

issues.title: Read settings from environment variables
issues.body: `config.load(path)` should let `FETCHIT_TIMEOUT` in the environment override the file and the defaults.
issues.check:
import os, tempfile
from fetchit import config
os.environ['FETCHIT_TIMEOUT'] = '3'
p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'none.ini')
assert str(config.load(p)['timeout']) == '3', config.load(p)

issues.title: Save the output to a file
issues.body: `fetchit URL --out result.json` should write the JSON to that file instead of printing it.

issues.title: Cache responses in memory
issues.body: `fetch_json(url, cache_seconds=30)` should return the earlier result for the same URL within 30 seconds, without fetching again.
issues.check:
import io, urllib.error
class Resp(io.BytesIO):
    def __enter__(self): return self
    def __exit__(self, *a): return False
from fetchit import fetch_json
calls = []
def op(req, timeout):
    calls.append(1)
    return Resp(b'{"n": 1}')
fetch_json('http://x.invalid/c', cache_seconds=30, opener=op)
fetch_json('http://x.invalid/c', cache_seconds=30, opener=op)
assert len(calls) == 1, calls

issues.title: Read the config from a YAML file
issues.body: `config.load` should also accept a `fetchit.yaml` file with a `fetchit:` mapping.
issues.check:
import os, tempfile
from fetchit import config
p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'fetchit.yaml')
open(p, 'w').write('fetchit:\n  timeout: 5\n')
assert str(config.load(p)['timeout']) == '5', config.load(p)

issues.title: Check required fields in the response
issues.body: `fetch_json(url, require=['id'])` should raise `FetchError` when the JSON object lacks any of the required keys.
